input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: Section 12.4 (second instance, p0046) imposes an undefined-scope, worldwide, all-product non-compete on Customer that survives 24 months post-term. That is walk-away territory under this rule (post-term restriction longer than 12 months and undefined scope, "any product or service that competes with Vendor"), and it fails every fallback element: it is not limited to a named competing product, is not term-only, exceeds 12 months, and carves out neither internal development nor acquisitions (it expressly bars acquiring competing products). It also directly contradicts § 12.3 (p0044), in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity or non-compete commitment. We therefore target the preferred position and replace the prohibition with a confirmation that no non-compete or field-of-use restriction applies. The separate no-hire covenant in the first § 12.4 (p0045) is a different commercial term and is left to the no-hire rule.

mappings.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.

proposal.summary: Replace the 24-month worldwide non-compete on Customer in § 12.4 with a confirmation that no non-compete or field-of-use restriction applies.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept restrictions on the products or services we may develop, buy, or sell, so we have removed the 24-month worldwide non-compete in § 12.4; it also contradicted § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no non-compete or exclusivity commitment.
